scholarships.title: Princeton University Need-Based Financial Aid Program (International Students)

existing.description: Princeton University operates a strictly need-based financial aid programme that it applies identically to international and domestic students. The full need of every admitted international student is met with grant aid, and Princeton's admission process is need-blind, so applying for aid carries no admission disadvantage. Since 2001 Princeton has replaced student loans with grants in the aid package, so no student is required to borrow. Aid covers tuition, room, board and other assessed costs of attendance. The Princeton Financial Aid Application is due November 9 for single-choice early action and February 1 for regular decision.
eligibility: Admitted Princeton undergraduate student, international or domestic
Same financial aid policy regardless of citizenship, citizenship status or ability to pay
Must complete the Princeton Financial Aid Application to be considered
Princeton does not offer academic or athletic merit scholarships
existing.eligibility_summary: All admitted Princeton students, including international students, are eligible for need-based financial aid. Princeton applies the same financial aid policy regardless of citizenship, citizenship status or ability to pay, and admission is need-blind. Aid is entirely need-based; Princeton does not offer academic or athletic merit scholarships.
benefits: Grant aid meeting 100% of demonstrated need
No student loans in the aid package since 2001
Same treatment for international students as for U.S. students
coverage: Books and personal expenses within the assessed cost of attendance
requirements: Submit the Common Application with Princeton-specific Questions
Submit the Princeton Financial Aid Application by Nov. 9 (single-choice early action) or Feb. 1 (regular decision)
Submit the Graded Written Paper in English
Submit an English proficiency test if applicable
Have school officials complete the School Report, School Counselor Letter and Final Report
Officially translate any non-English recommendation or school report
documents: School Report, School Counselor Letter and Transcript
TOEFL, IELTS Academic, Duolingo English Test or PTE Academic results if applicable
Official translations of non-English school documents
existing.english_requirement: Applicants whose native language is not English and who attend a school where English is not the language of instruction must take the TOEFL, IELTS Academic, the Duolingo English Test (DET) or the Pearson Test of English Academic (PTE Academic). These tests are not required if English is the applicant's native language or if the applicant has spent at least three years at a secondary school where English is the primary language of instruction.
application_method: Apply to Princeton through the Common Application with Princeton-specific Questions
Complete the Princeton Financial Aid Application, which is free and available to both U.S. and international applicants
Submit school reports and recommendations, with official translations if not in English
existing.selection_notes: Financial aid is awarded on demonstrated need only. Princeton states that if an applicant is admitted and has completed the Princeton Financial Aid Application, they will be notified of any aid award at the time admission is offered.
existing.best_fit: Admitted Princeton students from families unable to afford the full cost of attendance, including international applicants.
existing.notes: Princeton eliminated student loans from financial aid awards in 2001, replacing them with grants, and states no Princeton student has been required to borrow as part of a basic aid package. Financial aid awards cover the difference between Princeton's costs and the expected family contribution.
existing.duration: Four years of English (including continued practice in writing).
existing.application_period: Annual cycle. Single-choice early action application Nov. 1 with the financial aid application due Nov. 9; regular decision application Jan. 1 with the financial aid application due Feb. 1. Applications open in mid-August.
existing.deadline_display: Princeton publishes separate deadlines for the application and the aid form. Applications are due Nov. 1 (single-choice early action) or Jan. 1 (regular decision), and the Princeton Financial Aid Application is due Nov. 9 (single-choice early action) or Feb. 1 (regular decision).
existing.program_type: Need-based undergraduate financial aid programme (grant aid), not a merit scholarship
